quiz.q: Why do scholars characterize fascism as an unsystematic hodge-podge rather than a coherent political ideology?
options: Fascist leaders took power first and subsequently hired scholars to retrospectively rationalize their actions.
Fascist thinkers relied strictly on classical Marxist economic doctrines to plan their central state machinery.
Fascism emerged as an academic philosophical movement that failed to gain practical support among citizens.
Fascist regimes rejected all classical Western philosophers and developed entirely novel metaphysical theories from scratch.
quiz.why: Fascist ideology was constructed retrospectively after seizing power, with scholars hired to assemble borrowed ideas justifying state actions.

quiz.q: How does fascist political thought define the relationship between individual liberty and the state?
options: True liberty requires individuals to exercise universal human rights independently against state interference.
True liberty is realized solely through duty and complete submission under the authority of the state.
True liberty emerges when private market forces operate freely without corporate regulation by the state.
True liberty consists of direct democratic participation through regular parliamentary debates and public deliberation.
quiz.why: Fascism rejects individual rights against the state, maintaining that genuine liberty exists only through duty and obedience under state authority.

quiz.q: Why did Harold Laski and socialist scholars describe fascism as a counter-revolution?
options: It represented a popular revolution by trade unions to establish an egalitarian working-class state.
It abolished all private capital to replace bourgeois monopolies with worker-managed industrial syndicates.
It was sponsored by ruling elites to protect capitalism in crisis from growing socialist worker movements.
It transformed liberal constitutional democracies into egalitarian direct democracies driven by working-class solidarity.
quiz.why: Harold Laski argued that threatened capitalist elites backed fascist regimes to crush organized socialist labor and preserve capitalist power during crises.

quiz.q: According to Erich Fromm, which psychological tendency in human nature makes populations susceptible to fascism?
options: An innate drive for individual self-actualization through unconstrained democratic freedoms and civil liberties.
A rational desire to establish institutional checks and balances against centralized political authority.
A collective impulse to eliminate class hierarchies through peaceful deliberative consensus among citizens.
A subconscious fear of freedom and isolation that drives individuals to seek charismatic authority.
quiz.why: Erich Fromm argued that the psychological burden and isolation of freedom lead individuals to seek security in charismatic, authoritarian leaders.
